system.name: SPECTRA
system.one_liner: Training-free speculative decoding with a core module that mines guesses from the LLM itself and an optional retrieval module.

content.variant_note: an overview panel and a speedup chart on top; below, SPECTRA-CORE is paired with Lookahead decoding and SPECTRA-RETRIEVAL with REST in one drawing grammar, changed blocks labelled in red
content.argues: Optimized internal (core) and external (retrieval) speculation replace the matching blocks of Lookahead and REST and give the largest speedups across models.
content.subject: A HumanEval speedup chart, the SPECTRA overview and four sibling schematics pairing each earlier method with the proposed module.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw each baseline and the matching proposed module in one identical grammar side by side and colour only the labels of the blocks that changed, so the contribution is the visible difference; tie an overview panel to its detail panels with dotted arrows.
lessons.suits: Methods that upgrade specific components of a known pipeline (speculative decoding, retrieval, caching) where several baselines map onto the same skeleton.

evidence: Overview of Spectra and comparison with other non-training SOTA approaches.
We introduce SPECTRA (Figure 1a), a speculative decoding method that improves generation speed without requiring any training
The results in the bar chart are measured on HumanEval.

summary: SPECTRA speeds up LLM inference with speculative decoding that needs no training: a core module that mines guesses from the LLM's own predictions and an optional retrieval module. Figure 1 combines a HumanEval speedup bar chart (REST, ANPD, Lookahead and SPECTRA over four models, up to 3.0x) with a method overview (a) and four sibling schematics: SPECTRA-CORE (c) is paired with Lookahead decoding (b), SPECTRA-RETRIEVAL (e) with REST (d). All panels share one grammar of input, an LLM box with a token strip, guess grids, n-gram store or trie and corpus; blocks that are new in SPECTRA carry red labels, and dotted arrows tie the overview's modules to their detail panels.

notes: The colour roles of the token cells (blue input, purple candidate, peach guess) are read from the drawing and the arrows; the paper text given does not define them. The bar chart is one 234 x 69 pt bitmap, so its colours are approximate. The speedup chart is recorded under pictures, not as a panel, because it has no letter or frame.
